title: Probe Activation Matrix and Quant-Fallback Runbook
author: Aisha Rao
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the Probe Activation Matrix (PAM) — a deterministic policy that decides when to run targeted eval probes across hosted/dedicated/private fleets — and the accompanying Quant-Fallback Runbook used when quantization variants cause measurable quality regressions. PAM is intended to reduce eval noise, prioritize probes for customer-impacting SLOs, and automate safe fallback actions for quant migration.

Scope: applied-ml probes, runtime telemetry signals (latency, tail-pct, error-rate), quality signals from eval harness (delta-coherence, anchor-score), and quant variant rollout orchestrations. Does not replace the model-onboarding certification matrix but integrates with it via the "promotion hooks" section.

Owners and stakeholders

- Primary owner: Applied ML (probe-fabrication)
- Secondary owners: Serving Runtime (quant rollouts), Eng SRE (alerting & capacity), Product (SLO definition)
- Escalation contact: oncall-applied-ml -> oncall-eng-sre -> oncall-platform

Definitions and signals

- Probe: A synthetic, annotated input (usually from the probe registry) executed through the full serving stack and evaluated by the eval harness.
- Activation signal (examples):
  - SLO breach: production 99th latency > configured SLO by 20% for 5m.
  - Quality drift: rolling anchor-score delta > 0.08 vs baseline over 1h.
  - Quant anomaly: increase in token-level entropy variance combined with increased coherent-failure count.
- Probe priority classes: P0 (customer-visible SLA), P1 (high-risk slices), P2 (background/coverage), P3 (low-priority longtail)

Probe Activation Matrix (PAM) design

Goal: map runtime and quality signals to a minimal set of probes to run, with rules for escalation, sampling, and scheduled replays. PAM emits an activation manifest consumed by the eval-orchestrator.

Activation rules (summary):
1) Immediate activation (P0):
   - Trigger when any of: 99th latency > SLO*1.2 for 2 consecutive windows (5m each), or live anchor-score delta > 0.08 and user-impact flag true.
   - Probes: top 25 production-sampled probes for affected route + 5 targeted canary probes from the anchor family.
   - Run mode: high-fidelity (deterministic seeds, n=50 runs, mixed-quant variants enabled).

2) Priority activation (P1):
   - Trigger when: 95th latency increases > 15% or comp-similarity drift on an important slice is detected.
   - Probes: top 100 representative probes for slice, 10 targeted adversarial probes.
   - Run mode: fidelity medium (n=20, seeded), include quant baseline and current variant.

3) Scheduled regression scan (P2):
   - Trigger: daily background schedule or after model promotion from shadow -> canary.
   - Probes: stratified sample across tenant cohorts (n=500 total).
   - Run mode: low-fidelity (single run, mixed seeds).

4) Longtail harvest (P3):
   - Trigger: triggered by periodic annotation jobs or when storage backlog > 24h.
   - Probes: rare-slice catalog entries.

Activation manifest format (example JSON, emitted to eval-orchestrator):

{"manifest_id": "pam-2027-02-03-001", "trigger": "99p_latency_breach", "priority": "P0", "routes": ["/chat/generate"], "probe_sets": ["prod-top-25-20270203"], "run_mode": "high-fidelity", "include_quant_variants": ["fp16", "int8-q4_0", "int8-q5_1"]}

(Above is an example string; actual manifest is a simple key/value JSON sent to eval-orchestrator. See the eval-orchestrator API reference for schema.)

Telemetry-to-activation mapping (table)

Columns: signal | threshold | mapped-priority | probe-template
- 99p_latency | > SLO*1.2 (2x 5m windows) | P0 | prod-top-25 + anchor-canary
- anchor_score_delta | > 0.08 (1h) | P0 | anchor-family + adversarial-5
- 95p_latency | > +15% (1h) | P1 | slice-top-100
- token_entropy_var | > baseline*1.5 | P1 | quant-sensitivity-probe-set
- shadow_promotion | immediate | P2 | promotion-sanity-500

Probe run orchestration and resource constraints

- Rate limit: PAM must respect eval-fleet quotas. Default: 2000 probe-runs/hour cluster-wide.
- Priority preemption: P0 runs preempt lower-priority scheduled runs for up to 15 minutes; preemption is recorded in the manifest.
- Tenant isolation: never run tenant-owned probes of other customers without redaction. Use privacy-gated probes only.

Quant-Fallback Runbook (immediate steps)

When PAM detects a quality regression tied to a quant variant (observables: coherence drop, adversarial failure increase, or evaluator consensus change):

Immediate (0-30 minutes)
1) Triage: Applied ML oncall inspects activation manifest and runs the top-25 anchor probes locally with deterministic seeds across both baseline (fp16) and quant variant.
   - CLI (eval-orch):
     eval-orch run --manifest pam-XXX --probe-set prod-top-25 --seeds 0..49 --variants fp16,int8-q4_0 --output /tmp/pam-triage.json
2) If the quant variant shows > 7% absolute drop in anchor-score vs baseline (n>=30 runs), notify serving-runtime and create an incident: Incident template "quant-fallback-suspected".
3) Activate emergency fallback policy for affected routes: route-level config set to prefer baseline model or fp16 variant. This is a soft config that directs router to prefer non-quantized variants for new requests.
   - Example router command (gateway-admin):
     gateway-admin set-route-preference --route /chat/generate --prefer-variant fp16 --reason "quant regression" --expires 60m
4) Open a triage doc and tag: regression/quant-fallback + include manifest and triage outputs.

Short term remediation (30m-6h)
1) Run the extended quant-sensitivity suite (n=500 probes across slices) to measure scope.
2) If scope limited (single slice or route), apply targeted fallback (route or tenant-level). If broad, escalate to platform and prepare a global rollback plan.
3) Prepare a rollback change: rollback quant deployment in the release system (see rollback checklist below).

Rollback checklist (when fallback needed)

- Confirm regression signal across at least 2 independent telemetry sources (eval-harness, customer reports, and runtime error patterns).
- Post rollback impact assessment plan: run the promotion-sanity suite for 24h after rollback.
- Communication: notify CS and affected customers (template in communication playbook).
- Change window: prefer immediate for P0 customer-impacting regressions; schedule for maintenance window only for non-customer-visible regressions.

Post-incident actions (6h-2 weeks)

1) Root cause: collect seed-level diffs, token-level delta logs, and kv-cache hit/miss deltas. Attach to the triage doc.
2) If quant artifact is root cause, create a quant-variant-fix ticket with repro steps and quant-config used (scale, calibration tables, kernel flags).
3) Add a blocking probe to the promotion pipeline: any future promotion of that quant profile must pass the added blocking probe set with anchor-score within 0.03 of baseline.
4) Retro: run a postmortem with SLO impact calculation and update the PAM thresholds if signal-to-noise ratio was poor.

Promotion and onboarding hooks

- When a model/variant is promoted from shadow -> canary -> prod, the promotion pipeline must:
  1) Add a PAM activation entry: run promotion-sanity-500 on first 2h of canary traffic.
  2) Auto-schedule a P2 daily scan for the first 7 days post-promotion.
  3) If quant variant is enabled, attach the quant-sensitivity manifest and ensure evaluator seeds are locked for reproducibility.

Configuration examples

- Example quant-sensitivity probe-set description (text table):
  Name: quant-sensitivity-2027-01
  Targets: anchor-family (50), adversarial-20, topology-sensitive-30
  Run parameters: seeds 0..99, run_mode: mixed-fidelity

- Example fallback policy YAML (used by router/admin):

  route: "/chat/generate"
  fallback_priority: ["fp16", "fp32"]
  duration_minutes: 60
  reason: "auto-triggered quant fallback - anchor-score delta > 0.07"

Operational metrics and dashboards

- Minimum dashboards to maintain:
  - PAM Activations: count by priority, average time-to-start, manifest-to-complete latency.
  - Quant Regression Alerts: frequency, affected routes, percent-anchor-score-delta histogram.
  - Probe Fleet Utilization: concurrent runs, queue length, preemptions by priority.

Alerting thresholds (suggested)

- P0 activation: PagerDuty (Pager: pd-applied-ml) if anchor-score delta > 0.08 and >30% of anchor probes fail coherence checks.
- P1 activation: Email + Slack notification to #eval-harness for human review if 95p latency > 15% for 1h.
- Probe failures: SRE incident if >5% of scheduled probes fail due to infra issues for >10m.

Developer and runbook commands

- Quick triage run (single developer):
  eval-orch quick-run --probe-set anchor-canary --seeds 10 --variant int8-q5_1 --output s3://eval-artifacts/triage-{{ts}}
- Generate PAM manifest (local tester):
  python tools/pam/generate_manifest.py --signal 99p_latency_breach --route "/chat/generate" --priority P0 --out manifest.json

- Rollback (serving-runtime):
  rollout-admin rollback --deployment quant-deploy-20270129 --to-tag baseline-fp16 --force --comment "auto-rollback per PAM"

Privacy and safety constraints

- Use privacy-gated probes when tenant data is in the sample. Never activate privacy-gated probes in public eval clusters.
- For financial/health-related slices, escalate to Compliance before automated fallback is applied (manually review).

Appendix A: Probe naming conventions

- prod-top-N-YYYYMMDD: highest-fidelity production-sampled set for a route.
- anchor-family-XYZ: curated anchor probes for an intent family.
- quant-sensitivity-[id]: quant-specific adversarial/robustness probes.

Appendix B: Example log filter regexes

- Find anchor-score diffs: anchor_score_delta
- Runtime error patterns: ERROR\|model_timeout

Appendix C: Measurement templates (text)

- Anchor score report (columns): probe_id | baseline_score | variant_score | delta | n_runs
- Promotion sanity summary: route | baseline_latency_99p | variant_latency_99p | anchor_score_delta | quant_variant_id

References and related docs

- See: eval-orchestrator API (internal link), promotion-sanity checklist, quant-profile registry.
- See: related internal docs in the applied-ml-and-evals area for probe curation and quant profile synthesis.
